# Meal Manager

Meal Manager is a self-hosted family meal management app (inventory, recipes, weekly menus, shopping lists). It exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint so LLM agents can read a household's data on the user's behalf.

## How an LLM agent talks to Meal Manager

The app exposes a remote MCP server at `/mcp` (e.g. `https://your-domain.example/mcp`). Authentication is by Personal Access Token in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Tokens are scoped to a single household and revocable.

Thirteen tools cover inventory, recipes, weekly menus, shopping lists, ingredients catalog, household info, and recipe drafts. Most are read-only; three write to the household: `mealmanager_save_recipe_draft` saves a work-in-progress recipe draft to review, `mealmanager_create_ingredient` adds an ingredient to the catalog, and `mealmanager_add_inventory_item` adds (or increments) an item in the pantry, fridge or freezer. All tools are prefixed `mealmanager_`.

## Get a token

A user creates a token from `/settings/tokens` after signing in. The plaintext is shown once and never persisted in clear (only its SHA-256 hash is stored).

## Pointers

- Full agent-facing doc: [/llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt)
- MCP endpoint: [/mcp](/mcp)
- API catalog (RFC 9727): [/.well-known/api-catalog](/.well-known/api-catalog)
- OpenAPI 3.1 of the MCP endpoint: [/openapi-mcp.yaml](/openapi-mcp.yaml)
- Bot policy: [/robots.txt](/robots.txt) — all AI crawlers are disallowed on HTML pages; the only legitimate agent channel is `/mcp` with a Bearer PAT.
- Source: spec-driven via OpenSpec, hexagonal architecture per bounded context.
